messages.author: dc4c0551de20bad6
messages.subject: SRMSR Differences with QMC=T
parts:
Greetings, I've been advised to focus on the SRMSR value for a five-factor confirmatory multidimensional graded response model. Some of my factors are highly correlated (.82 and .76), but exploratory mgrms and CFA suggest that five factors still provide the best fit. 

I understand that I should be using QMC=T, but I'm trying to understand why my residual correlations increase so much with this method. Any insights would be appreciated. Here are my fit indices before I start trimming items. 

M2(mod2, theta_lim=c(-4,4),QMC=T)
            M2          df   p      RMSEA    RMSEA_5   RMSEA_95         SRMSR       TLI      
stats 2498.519 656 0 0.07722245 0.07394511 0.08036141 0.2507739 0.9317036 
CFI  
0.935721

M2(mod2, theta_lim=c(-4,4),QMC=F)
            M2           df p      RMSEA    RMSEA_5   RMSEA_95      SRMSR       TLI      
stats 1700.102 656 0 0.05813117 0.05468878 0.06146621 0.09390705 0.9612984 
CFI  
0.963575

Thanks, 
Gary

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: SRMSR Differences with QMC=T
parts:
The form without QMC=TRUE is likely imprecise due to very grainy approximations of the numerical integrals (hence, fit indices are unreliably too high/low). The Quasi-Monte Carlo approach is better in that the integration is generally more reliable given the dimensionality of your problem. HTH.

Phil
